zh.principle: **攻击**：恩尼格玛破译（Enigma Cryptanalysis）。计算机历史博物馆时间线对英国“Bombe”的条目写道：「Built as an electro-mechanical means of decrypting Nazi ENIGMA-based military communications during World War II, the British Bombe is conceived of by computer pioneer Alan Turing and Harold Keen of the British Tabulating Machine Company.Hundreds of allied bombes were built in order to determine the daily rotor start positions of Enigma cipher machines, which in turn allowed the Allies to decrypt German messages.」破译的关键目标是复原每日转子起始位置。
zh.why: 同一时间线条目把方法来源写清楚：「The basic idea for bombes came from Polish code-breaker Marian Rejewski's 1938 "Bomba."」——英国装置是在波兰先行工作之上扩展的。布莱奇利园官方网站的 Enigma 摘要则说明机器本身：「The Enigma machine was invented by a German engineer Arthur Scherbius shortly after WW1.The machine (of which a number of varying types were produced) …」，即机型多样、需按型号处理。
zh.used: 规模是两个来源共同强调的：布莱奇利园页面写明「Nearly 10,000 people worked in the wider Bletchley Park organisation」，其 Bombe 摘要称「These Alan Turing-designed devices changed the course of the Second World War, saving millions of lives in the process」；CHM 条目则给出机器数量与效果：「Hundreds of allied bombes were built … which in turn allowed the Allies to decrypt German messages」。
zh.broken: 这条路径的局限也写在文本里：Bombe 的工作方式是搜索「daily rotor start positions」，即逐日确定转子起始位置；同时布莱奇利园页面是面向公众的导览摘要（站点保存内容为摘要布局，完整叙事文本不在该页），该条目因此只采用其中可核对的句子，不把它当作技术论文的替代。
zh.history:
时间线上的锚点是 1941 年：「The first Bombe is completed」，且波兰 1938 年的 Bomba 提供了基本思想；布莱奇利园自身的介绍页面把图灵列为在该园工作过的最知名破译人员之一，并把整段历史概括为这处园区对盟军胜利至关重要。

en.principle: **Attack**: Enigma Cryptanalysis (恩尼格玛破译). The Computer History Museum timeline describes the British Bombe: "Built as an electro-mechanical means of decrypting Nazi ENIGMA-based military communications during World War II, the British Bombe is conceived of by computer pioneer Alan Turing and Harold Keen of the British Tabulating Machine Company. Hundreds of allied bombes were built in order to determine the daily rotor start positions of Enigma cipher machines, which in turn allowed the Allies to decrypt German messages." The target of the operation was recovering the daily rotor start positions.
en.why: The same timeline entry records the lineage of the method: “The basic idea for bombes came from Polish code-breaker Marian Rejewski's 1938 "Bomba."” — the British device extended earlier Polish work. The Bletchley Park Trust site's Enigma summary describes the machine itself: "The Enigma machine was invented by a German engineer Arthur Scherbius shortly after WW1. The machine (of which a number of varying types were produced) …", noting multiple variants that had to be handled.
en.used:
Both sources stress scale. The Bletchley Park page states that "Nearly 10,000 people worked in the wider Bletchley Park organisation", and its Bombe summary says "These Alan Turing-designed devices changed the course of the Second World War, saving millions of lives in the process". The CHM entry gives the machine count and the effect: "Hundreds of allied bombes were built … which in turn allowed the Allies to decrypt German messages".

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken: The limits of this route are visible in the wording: the Bombe worked by searching "daily rotor start positions", that is, determining the rotor start positions day by day. The Bletchley Park page is also a public visitor summary — the saved content is the site's summary layout, with the full narrative absent — so this entry uses only its checkable sentences and does not treat it as a substitute for a technical account.

zh: 恩尼格玛：德国使用的转子密码机族。
Bombe：用于搜索恩尼格玛每日转子起始位置的机电设备。
Bomba：波兰 1938 年的先行装置。
转子起始位置：每日密钥状态的一部分。
每日更换：转子起始位置需要逐日重新确定。
盟军解密：由破译转子状态得知的德军通信可读结果。
en: Enigma: the family of German rotor cipher machines.
Bombe: the electro-mechanical device searching Enigma rotor start positions.
Rotor start positions: part of the daily key state.
Daily change: the rotor start positions had to be recovered afresh each day.
Allied decrypts: readable German messages resulting from the breaks.
